rows.definition: The generic engineering abstraction: sense -> decide -> act -> witness, at any altitude (tool-call / turn / session / fleet / RSI / intent).
rows.distinction: The SHAPE every named mechanism instantiates - NOT any one of them (fak loop the ledger, superloop the walker, loopgate the gate); the abstraction, not a subsystem.

rows.definition: A read-only operator-INTENT walker: an interior node that reads its member loops' status worst-first and folds a worklist, mutating nothing at its own altitude.
rows.distinction: A read-only INTENT walker (interior node, spawns nothing) - NOT the /super-loop skill (a bulk detached wave LAUNCHER that spawns fleets) and NOT a normal leaf loop (which ticks and does one task).

rows.definition: The durable hash-chained loop ledger (.fak/loops.jsonl) plus the admission governor (loopmgr.Admit): it records loop events and folds them into an advisory admit/refuse, it does not schedule or spawn.
rows.distinction: A RECORD + admission gate over one loop's events - NOT fak loop drive (an actual Ralph loop) and NOT loopfleet (the cross-ledger health fold over MANY loops).

rows.definition: The actual iterating loop: re-reads a GOAL.md goal-spec fresh each turn and drives to a witnessed_done verdict or a spent budget - the one mechanism in the family that genuinely loops.
rows.distinction: An ACTUAL loop that settles one GOAL.md witness - NOT fak loop (the ledger + governor, which only records and gates) and NOT a super loop (an intent walker over other loops).

rows.definition: The cross-ledger loop-health FOLD (internal/loopfleet): rolls up the loopmgr / nightrun / dojo / cadence / dispatch ledgers into one live / stale / dark view of every loop.
rows.distinction: A READ-ONLY fold over MANY loops' ledgers - NOT loopmgr (governs ONE loop's admission) and NOT loophealth (a single loop's per-row state that loopfleet consumes).

rows.definition: The per-loop health record (state, runs, keep-rate, dark flag) that the loopfleet fold produces for a single ledgered loop.
rows.distinction: ONE loop's rolled-up health row - NOT loopfleet (the fold that produces many of them) and NOT loopscore (the durability scorecard over the loop set).

rows.definition: The Orient->Plan->Act->Verify->Ship->Learn STAGE-coverage scorecard (fak loop-index-scorecard): are the agentic-coding loop stages witnessed at floor.
rows.distinction: A STAGE-coverage scorecard (which loop stages are covered) - NOT an index OF loops (that role is the loop-family map doc) and NOT loopscore (loop durability, not stage coverage).

rows.definition: The durability scorecard (internal/loopscore): are firing loops registered, non-dark, outcome-recorded, and guard-wrapped.
rows.distinction: A DURABILITY scorecard (is a loop registered + non-dark + witnessed) - NOT loop-index (stage coverage) and NOT loopfleet (the live health fold it reads).

rows.definition: The benchmark control surface (internal/benchloop): folds the benchmark registry + run catalog + nightrun ledger into the single next benchmark action.
rows.distinction: The BENCHMARK control surface (what benchmark to run next) - NOT loopbench (internal/loopgate/loopbench.go, the verified-vs-naive exit-gate micro-bench) - unrelated code paths sharing a spelling.

rows.definition: The always-on background-loop supervisor (internal/bgloop, fak bgloop) that keeps a detached loop process alive across restarts.
rows.distinction: The PROCESS babysitter (keep a detached loop alive) - NOT fak loop (the ledger) and NOT a super loop (an intent walker); bgloop owns the process lifecycle, not the work selection.

rows.definition: The recovery path (internal/looprecover, fak loop recover) that reconciles a loop's ledger after a crash so a resumed loop does not double-count or lose its in-flight run.
rows.distinction: Ledger RECONCILIATION after a crash - NOT bgloop (keeps the process alive in the first place) and NOT loopmgr (the steady-state governor).

rows.definition: The recursive-self-improvement loop (internal/rsiloop): proposes a change, measures a witness-verified metric gain, and keeps-or-reverts on a non-forgeable keep-bit.
rows.distinction: A KEEP-OR-REVERT improvement loop (measure gain, keep the winner) - NOT loop drive (settles a GOAL.md witness, no keep-bit) and NOT a super loop (an intent walker that mutates nothing).

rows.definition: The package (internal/loopmap, fak loopmap) that renders the loop-family map: which mechanism plays which role (timer / selector / executor / witness) and where the names collide.
rows.distinction: A MAP of the loop mechanisms and their roles - NOT loop-index (stage coverage of one loop) and NOT loopfleet (the live health fold); loopmap is the taxonomy, not a live status read.

rows.definition: The audit pass over a loop's ledger that checks a run's claimed outcome against its witnessed evidence (was a done actually witnessed).
rows.distinction: An AUDIT of ledger claims vs witnesses - NOT loopscore (the aggregate durability grade) and NOT looprecover (crash reconciliation); the audit reads, it does not repair.
gaps: the loop-ledger audit pass is not yet written into the concept glossary

rows.definition: The identity binding one loop RUN to a work session, so a resumed or re-dispatched run keeps a stable session identity across the ledger.
rows.distinction: One RUN's session identity - NOT loopmgr (the governor over all a loop's runs) and NOT loopdrive (the driver that produces runs); loopsession is the per-run key.
gaps: the per-run loop-session identity is not yet written into the concept glossary

rows.definition: The resolver (defaultLoopPolicy) for where the loop admission policy lives: FAK_LOOP_POLICY, else .fak/loop-policy.json - the file loopmgr.LoadPolicies reads to brake a background loop.
rows.distinction: The POLICY-FILE path resolver (where backpressure config lives) - NOT loopmgr.Admit (the gate that enforces it) and NOT defaultLoopRegistry (the loop job registry path).
gaps: the loop admission-policy path resolver is not yet written into the concept glossary

rows.definition: The networking term: the 127.0.0.1 loopback address / same-host bind (isLoopback, loopbackOnly), swallowed by the `loop` root but from a different domain entirely.
rows.distinction: A NETWORKING term (same-host address) - NOT any work-loop concept; drawn here only because the `loop` root collides with the address family name.
